issue: Draft/bot gate relaxations in Pipeline are keyed only on self_driving, not coupled to pr.author_is_bot

verdicts.evidence: tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225 (bot refusal relaxed by flag), review_pr.py:590 (draft gate relaxed by flag alone, not conditioned on author_is_bot); products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-172 (webhook leg enforces _is_bot_authored) vs tasks.py:1110-1232 (receiver leg process_inbox_pr_review stamps inbox_review with NO author check on the fetched PR — bot authorship is docstring-only at tasks.py:1117); products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:159,185,203-212 (backstop stamps output.pr_url by branch match with no author check, so a human-opened PR from the agent's repo-native branch can become the run's pr_url); products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 → tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321 (flag flows to the engine); tasks.py:225-229 (_review_skip_reason docstring: "The engine keeps the same bot/draft refusals as defense in depth" — the invariant the PR's carve-out no longer guarantees).
verdicts.notes: The finding's code claim is correct and the common refutation ("no caller can set self_driving=True for a non-bot PR") does not hold: the receiver leg (process_inbox_pr_review) never verifies the fetched PR's author, and the tasks webhook backstop stamps pr_url purely on a head-branch match, so on the public repo a human-authored PR opened from the agent's work branch can reach the engine with self_driving=True. In that state the draft gate silently disappears and the reviewer prompt carries trusted task provenance for a PR whose title/body/base are human-controlled. The one-line fail-closed guard (disable self_driving when pr.author_is_bot is False after fetch) matches the codebase's explicit belt-and-braces doctrine and closes the gap at the layer upstream code documents as defense in depth. must_fix is overblown though: the bad path needs an opted-in acting reviewer, an unstamped pr_url race, and still passes every other gate plus the LLM verdict over agent-pushed diff content — real but limited, hence should_fix.

verdicts.evidence: tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590 (`if pr.draft and not self.self_driving:`) and :225 (`if self.pr.author_is_bot and not self.self_driving:`) — each gate tests its own subject; self_driving relaxes both. No caller can set self_driving=True on a non-bot PR: review_pr.py:973-984 main() never passes the flag (no --self-driving CLI arg), and the sole producer chain is review_local.py:321 `self_driving=bool(context.get("self_driving_review"))` ← products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, stamped only on runs positively linked to signals implementation tasks, which open bot-authored draft PRs by construction (Pipeline.__init__ docstring, review_pr.py:202-209).
verdicts.notes: The finding's trigger is explicitly "a caller-side bug that sets self_driving=True without author_is_bot also being true" — a hypothetical the current call sites rule out. Even if it fired, the bypass only skips the draft caution prerequisite in _check_prerequisites (review_pr.py:584-607); deny-list, size, tier gates and the LLM review still run and can REFUSE/ESCALATE, so it is not an approval-forcing gate. The suggested compound condition is redundant defensive coupling of two independent gates. Classic defensive-paranoia / speculative what-if; drop.

verdicts.evidence: Engine premise confirmed: tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py ~line 225 relaxes the bot-author refusal on `if self.pr.author_is_bot and not self.self_driving`, and _check_prerequisites (~line 590) relaxes the draft gate on `if pr.draft and not self.self_driving` — no binding of the flag to pr.author_is_bot anywhere in the engine. Flag flows: review_local.py:321 `self_driving=bool(context.get("self_driving_review"))` ← activities.py:451 `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`. The webhook leg does positively gate bot authorship (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169 `if not _is_bot_authored(pr): return _InboxCarveOut()` plus repo-native-head check at :177-178), but the receiver leg process_inbox_pr_review (tasks.py:1110-1240) stamps `output={"inbox_review": ...}` (tasks.py:1229) with NO bot-author, draft-shape, or run-linkage check — its "bot-authored by construction" docstring rests on the caller-controlled pr_url (the confirmed T7 gap). So a human-authored draft PR reaching the engine with self_driving=True is reachable today, but only via T7's server-side hole.
verdicts.notes: T6 is real as a code fact and its scenario is currently reachable, but it is derivative of T7 (the must_fix in this set): the root cause and correct fix is server-side re-attestation in process_inbox_pr_review, not the engine. The suggested engine-level `self_driving and author_is_bot` bind would only block the human-authored-draft variant of the exploit while leaving the worse variant (unearned approval of an arbitrary bot-authored PR, e.g. dependabot) open, and becomes redundant once T7 is fixed. It does align with the codebase's stated defense-in-depth stance (tasks.py `_review_skip_reason` comment: "The engine keeps the same bot/draft refusals as defense in depth") and PR data is already in hand, so it is a valid, cheap hardening — worth a consider, not a standalone should/must_fix. The prior verifier's "unreachable through actual call sites" rebuttal in setT.md is wrong because it accepted the receiver leg's "bot-authored by construction" docstring, which T7's verified analysis (same document) refutes.

verdicts.evidence: Flag has exactly one setter, fully server-derived: products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 sets self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review")) from the ReviewRun DB row. inbox_review is stamped only by two provenance-verified paths: the inbox trigger (tasks.py:1176-1229) and _inbox_rereview_carve_out (tasks.py:144-217), which enforces fork-safety (head repo must equal base repo, tasks.py:177-179), enabled+synced config, a team-scoped tasks-facade match with an explicit run.team_id == repo_config.team_id recheck (tasks.py:201-202), and an opted-in acting reviewer. No GitHub-controlled field (pr.title/body/reviews/discussion) flows into the flag; those are separate context keys built server-side. The engine-side gates (review_pr.py:225, review_local.py:321-326) do trust the flag, but the sandbox is tokenless by design and the server is the documented trust authority.
verdicts.notes: The finding concedes its own emptiness: "No reachable vulnerability exists today" and "defense-in-depth around a deliberate design decision, not a claim the current server derivation is wrong." The entire risk is conditioned on a hypothetical future caller setting the flag or a future refactor sourcing it from GitHub data — ruled out by the single, well-commented, provenance-keyed setter in current code. The "expanded untrusted-content surface" (bot PRs reaching the LLM) is the intended feature, already covered by _sanitize_untrusted and the anti-injection notice per the finding itself. Speculative future-proofing, not a current defect.

verdicts.evidence: reviewer.py:692 gates the trusted "author is a machine user" block on cl["self_driving"] alone; review_pr.py:590 relaxes the draft gate on the same flag; review_local.py:321-326 takes the flag verbatim from context JSON and skips the bot-author refusal, never cross-checking pr.author_is_bot. The bot-author invariant is NOT airtight upstream: process_inbox_pr_review (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1240) stamps inbox_review without any author check (unlike the webhook re-review leg, which requires _is_bot_authored), and its pr_url comes from TaskRun.output.pr_url (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93), which the tasks webhook backstop _record_run_pr_url (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py, handle_pull_request_event) writes for ANY repo-native PR matched by branch+repo — no author check. A write-access human opening a PR from the agent's pushed work branch (when agent-side detection missed, the exact case the backstop exists for) yields self_driving=True on a human-authored PR.
verdicts.notes: The finding framed the trigger as a hypothetical server mis-stamp, but a concrete instantiation exists: human opens PR from the task's work branch -> tasks webhook backstop binds it to the run by branch+repo -> review_hog receiver queues process_inbox_pr_review -> engine gets self_driving=True on a human PR, relaxing the draft gate on a branch-protection-counting approval and injecting a false trusted claim ("author is a machine user, draft state is not a caution signal"). Requires opted-in acting reviewer + missed agent PR detection + insider with write access, and the LLM still reviews the real diff, so damage is degraded review integrity rather than automatic approval -> should_fix, not must_fix. The suggested fix (gate both carve-outs on self_driving AND pr.author_is_bot) is a one-line engine-side re-assertion that preserves the intended flow. Note: this contradicts the prior dismissed verdict in setV.md, whose "bot author by construction" claim overlooked the branch-matched webhook backstop leg.

verdicts.evidence: review_pr.py:590 `if pr.draft and not self.self_driving` — bypass exists as described. But no reachable input sets self_driving on a human draft: (a) review_pr.py main() constructs Pipeline without self_driving (CLI args only), so the Action path never sets it; (b) the sole production setter is review_local.py:321 `self_driving=bool(context.get("self_driving_review"))`, fed by activities.py:451 `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`; (c) inbox_review provenance is stamped only at tasks.py:880 (webhook carve-out, which hard-gates `if not _is_bot_authored(pr): return _InboxCarveOut()` at tasks.py:169 plus repo-native head check at 176-178) and tasks.py:1176 (process_inbox_pr_review, whose pr_url is the triggering signal-report TaskRun's own output.pr_url — written only by the agent server for the bot-opened PR or by products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:179-185, which requires head repo == base repo and only backfills when output.pr_url is unset). The failure scenario is explicitly conditioned on a hypothetical upstream "construction bug", not on any actual input.
verdicts.notes: The suggested `self_driving and pr.author_is_bot` effective-flag is pure defense-in-depth over bot-author invariants the two provenance producers already enforce; for a hypothetically mis-flagged human PR the bot-refusal branch (review_pr.py:225) is already a no-op and a GitHub draft cannot merge while draft. Speculative what-if, not a production defect this PR introduces.

verdicts.evidence: review_pr.py:225 (`if self.pr.author_is_bot and not self.self_driving`) and :590 (`if pr.draft and not self.self_driving`) relax both gates on one flag; review_local.py:321 sets it verbatim from `context.get("self_driving_review")` with no cross-check against `_build_pr_data`'s `author_is_bot`. The mis-set-flag precondition is reachable, not hypothetical: tasks facade api.py:1773-1788 lets a task:write caller repoint `output.pr_url` (shape-only validation, api.py:1940); review_hog receivers.py:93,126-139,225 forwards it unverified; stamphog tasks.py:1110-1234 (`process_inbox_pr_review`) checks only repo-config-enabled + PR open + head_sha — no `_is_bot_authored`, no fork check, no pr_url↔task_run linkage verification — and stamps `inbox_review` (line 1229); activities.py:451 turns that into `self_driving_review=True` in the sandbox context. A prompt-injected sandbox agent can therefore point the run at a human-authored draft PR in the connected repo and have the engine waive the draft prerequisite en route to a real APPROVE. The proposed engine guard (`self_driving and pr.author_is_bot`) would block that specific chain because the context's author data comes from a live GitHub fetch of the actual PR (activities.py:434-451).
verdicts.notes: Real defense-in-depth gap on a concretely reachable attack path, but must_fix overstates it: the root defect is the receiver leg's missing verification (same chain as finding N10), whose fix closes this scenario; the bot-author-refusal half of the relaxation is inert for non-bot authors (only the draft waiver is behaviorally live); and the suggested guard is partial (PRData has no head-repo field, so bot-authored fork PRs still pass). The webhook re-review path already validates bot/fork/linkage — only the initial receiver leg lacks it.

verdicts.evidence: review_pr.py:225 and :590 match the finding's description (draft/bot gates keyed on self.self_driving alone). But the flag reaches the engine only via bool(output.get("inbox_review")) (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451, review_local.py:321), and both stamping paths enforce bot authorship: the webhook carve-out checks _is_bot_authored(pr) (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169), fork safety (:176-178), team-scoped run match + recheck (:191-200), and toggle (:205-207) on every head-changing delivery; the initial leg (process_inbox_pr_review, tasks.py:1109-1133) fires only for the signals run's own bot-opened PR. The finding's concrete trigger (human pushes to the bot's branch) keeps author_is_bot=True (PR author = opener), so the suggested guard `author_is_bot and self_driving` behaves identically in that scenario — the fix doesn't address its own example. Replays are guarded by the payload_updated_at stale-snapshot recheck (tasks.py:1190-1197) and select_for_update dedupe (:1202-1207). The draft gate is a policy gate (tasks.py:227 "reviewing one now is wasted"), not the security boundary.
verdicts.notes: No reachable path produces self_driving=True with author_is_bot=False absent an upstream bug; remaining triggers are speculative. The suggested combined guard is legitimate cheap defense-in-depth at the server-to-sandbox context boundary, but hardening, not a defect this PR introduces. (Closest residual edge: tasks/webhooks.py:184-185 backstop could bind a same-repo human-opened PR to a run pre-detection — internal write-access actor only, not the finding's scenario.)

this_experiment_findings.title: Do not bypass the draft gate for non-bot authors
this_experiment_findings.problem: The self-driving flag disables the draft prerequisite for every PR, not only bot-authored PRs. If the flag is set incorrectly, a human-authored draft can receive an approval while the trusted prompt incorrectly states that the author is a machine user and that draft status is not a caution signal.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Enforce the invariant at the gate boundary. For example, bypass the draft check only when `self.self_driving and pr.author_is_bot`, and reject or ignore `self_driving` for human-authored PRs. Apply the same validation in `review_local.py` so the offline and hosted paths cannot diverge.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Claims the Pipeline draft-gate bypass is keyed on self_driving alone and proposes `self_driving and pr.author_is_bot`, which is exactly cluster 6's 'draft/bot gate relaxations keyed only on self_driving, not coupled to pr.author_is_bot' at the review_pr.py:590 draft gate; rejected cluster 5 because the machine-author prompt text is only cited as a consequence, not the defect.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Traced every setter of the flag from the engine gate back to its origin (worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):

- tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590 `if pr.draft and not self.self_driving:` — the gate under review. review_pr.py:196/209 is the only way to set it (constructor kwarg); review_pr.py:975-984 (the Action CLI `main`) has no `--self-driving` argument and constructs `Pipeline(args.pr_number, args.repo, dry_run=..., verbose=...)`, so the Action path can never set it.
- tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321 `Pipeline(..., self_driving=bool(context.get("self_driving_review")))`; review_local.py:324 applies the same bot-author guard, and `_run_gates_offline` reuses `_check_prerequisites`, so hosted and offline paths already share one draft gate (the finding's "cannot diverge" ask is already the state of the code).
- products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:448-451 sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))` and nothing else.
- `inbox_review` is stamped in two places only: (a) the webhook carve-out, products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-172 `if not _is_bot_authored(pr): return _InboxCarveOut()` before any provenance is built (tasks.py:206-213) — a human-authored PR cannot receive provenance there; (b) products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1176-1182 in `process_inbox_pr_review`, which fetches the PR by URL and does not check authorship. That URL comes from `TaskRun.output["pr_url"]` (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:84-85, 127-138), which products/tasks/backend/temporal/code_workstreams/activities/load_pr_urls.py:26-29 documents as user-writable.
- products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:92-98 states the design: the engine flag is set exclusively from persisted inbox provenance, which the trigger paths stamp only after linkage verification; the engine is not the place that verifies linkage.
- tools/pr-approval-agent/test_review_pr.py:569-600 pins the current gate contract (self-driving reviews drafts; CHANGES_REQUESTED still blocks).
fresh_votes.refutation: The premise ("the flag is set incorrectly for a human-authored PR") is only reachable through one hole: `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1110-1245) stamps `inbox_review` on whatever open PR a user-writable `TaskRun.output.pr_url` points at, without verifying bot authorship or run linkage. That is exactly finding UA7 in the same file, validated as must_fix at the layer where the trust decision is made (run creation). The webhook stamper already refuses human authors at tasks.py:169, and the Action path never sets the flag at all. The engine-side change UA1 proposes (`self_driving and pr.author_is_bot` at review_pr.py:590) is a second, partial copy of that boundary: it would not stop the mis-provenanced ReviewRun from being created, would not restore the server-side write-permission/review-mode gates bypassed at tasks.py:944/968, and would not fix the misleading prompt because `classification["self_driving"]` (review_pr.py:477) would still be True. The offline/hosted divergence the finding warns about does not exist — review_local.py already runs the same `_check_prerequisites`. So UA1 is a duplicated, weaker safeguard for a defect already reported at the correct place, not an independent reachable bug in the draft gate.

fresh_votes.evidence: Worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215. The draft bypass at tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590 (`if pr.draft and not self.self_driving`) and the bot-author bypass at :225 key off the same flag, which defaults closed (`self_driving: bool = False`, :196). The flag is set in exactly two places: tools/pr-approval-agent/review_local.py:321 from `context.get("self_driving_review")`, and products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 from `bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`. `inbox_review` provenance is stamped only by (a) the webhook carve-out, which returns empty unless `_is_bot_authored(pr)` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-171) and the head repo is repo-native (:176-178) and the tasks facade positively links the PR to a non-internal signal-report run (:191-200), and (b) `process_inbox_pr_review` (tasks.py:1176-1182), which is only reached via review_hog's TaskRun receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:72-138) using the `pr_url` written into the output of a non-internal, signal-report-carrying implementation TaskRun (:97-104) - i.e. a PR opened by the task runtime's machine user. Existing tests already pin the gate behavior: tools/pr-approval-agent/test_review_pr.py:569-586 parametrize the draft gate over self_driving (normal run blocks drafts, self-driving reviews them), :589-594 confirm the carve-out relaxes only the draft issue (CHANGES_REQUESTED still blocks), and tools/pr-approval-agent/test_review_local.py:283-315 verify an Action-shaped context (no `self_driving_review` key) keeps the harness gates while a self-driving context reviews the bot-authored draft. products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:92-99 documents the flag as set exclusively from persisted inbox provenance stamped only by linkage-verified trigger paths.
fresh_votes.refutation: The finding's premise is "if the flag is set incorrectly", i.e. corrupted or forged trusted server provenance. No code path sets self_driving=True for a human-authored PR: the engine never sets it itself, the hosted activity derives it from ReviewRun.output["inbox_review"], and both stampers of that provenance either check bot authorship explicitly (webhook carve-out, tasks.py:169) or obtain the PR URL from the machine-authored implementation run's own output (receiver leg). The suggested `self.self_driving and pr.author_is_bot` guard in the engine would only change behavior in a state the system cannot produce, making it a duplicated safeguard rather than a fix for a reachable defect. The one real gap in this area - `process_inbox_pr_review` not re-verifying the fetched PR's author/linkage before stamping provenance - is a different, provenance-boundary concern already captured as finding UA7, not the engine draft gate cited here. Existing tests already lock the intended gate semantics on both the Action and hosted paths.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Engine: `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225` (`if self.pr.author_is_bot and not self.self_driving`) and `:590` (`if pr.draft and not self.self_driving`) relax both gates on the flag alone; `review_local.py:321` sets it from `context["self_driving_review"]`; `reviewer.py:683-699` then tells the model "The author is a machine user" whenever `classification["self_driving"]` is set, with no `author_is_bot` check anywhere in the engine.

Server-side, the flag comes only from `output["inbox_review"]` (`products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451`). That provenance is stamped by two legs. The webhook re-review leg does enforce the invariant: `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` returns empty unless `_is_bot_authored(pr)` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:174-177`). The initial-review leg does not: `process_inbox_pr_review` (`tasks.py:1110-1245`) fetches the PR and stamps `inbox_review` at `:1176-1182`/`:1229` with no author check; the receiver that queues it (`products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:72-140`) only requires `task.signal_report_id` set, `task.internal` false and the toggle on.

A human-authored PR on such a task is reachable in production configuration, though only by a deliberate off-UI API call: the Inbox UI creates the task with `origin_product=signal_report` and runs it with `run_source=signal_report` (`frontend/src/scenes/inbox/inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:80-96`), which forces BOT authorship (`products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:3039`). But the same task creator can instead call the run endpoint with `run_source=manual` and `pr_authorship_mode=user` (or a `github_user_token`): the BOT override is skipped (`facade/api.py:3039` only fires for `run_source == SIGNAL_REPORT`), `_resolve_cloud_pr_authorship_mode` accepts USER for the task creator with a usable GitHub integration and skips all checks when a caller token is given (`facade/api.py` `_resolve_cloud_pr_authorship_mode`), and `get_pr_authorship_mode` returns `run_state.pr_authorship_mode` before it consults `task.origin_product` (`products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/utils.py:1067-1071`). `TaskWriteSerializer.validate` rejects `github_user_integration` on signal-report tasks (`serializers.py:640-646`) but nothing rejects a later user-authored run on them. Result: a non-internal task with `signal_report_id`, a PR pushed under the human's identity, the receiver fires, `process_inbox_pr_review` stamps provenance, and the engine reviews a human-authored (possibly draft) PR while its prompt asserts the author is a machine user.
fresh_votes.refutation: The validator's refutation holds for every path the UI and auto-start produce: `auto_start.py:250-261` and the Inbox kickoff both force BOT authorship, and `products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:92` plus the `activities.py:447-451` comment state that provenance is the sole authorization boundary. I also checked whether the webhook leg would mask the gap: it does check `_is_bot_authored` (`tasks.py:174-177`), so any later push on a human-authored PR falls back to the normal path and its head-changing retraction dismisses the draft approval. The only trigger left needs the PR's own author, already a team member with tasks access and repo push rights, to hand-craft a run request that swaps authorship to themselves; the outcome is a self-driving-framed Stamphog review of their own draft PR in their own repo, head-pinned and retracted on the next push. No third party can induce it, and the reviewer still judges the diff. So the claimed must_fix security hole does not exist, but the invariant "inbox provenance implies bot author" is enforced on one server leg and not the other, and the engine trusts it blindly, which is a real if minor gap. The better fix is server-side parity (mirror `_is_bot_authored` in `process_inbox_pr_review`) rather than the engine-side check the finding proposes.

this_experiment_findings.title: Limit the draft bypass to bot-authored PRs
this_experiment_findings.problem: The self-driving flag bypasses the draft gate for every author. A linked context for a human-authored draft can therefore reach review and receive an approval. The initial Inbox review path does not verify that GitHub reports a bot author before it sets this flag.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Fail closed when `self_driving` is true but `pr.author_is_bot` is false. Also require the context producer to verify the bot author and repository-native head before it creates the review run.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Claims the engine's draft-gate bypass at review_pr.py:587-590 keys only on self_driving without requiring pr.author_is_bot, which is cluster 6's exact claim; cluster 2 rejected because SB4's anchor and fix are the Pipeline gate, with the receiver-leg bot check only as a secondary remark.

Premise traced from the engine gate back to its callers, all under /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215:

1. Engine: tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:590 `if pr.draft and not self.self_driving:` skips the draft prerequisite for any author, and review_pr.py:225 `if self.pr.author_is_bot and not self.self_driving:` only refuses bots. No branch anywhere in review_pr.py / review_local.py (review_local.py:321-326 mirrors it) fails closed on `self_driving and not author_is_bot`. Initial (receiver) path stamps `inbox_review` without any author check: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1131-1180 (`process_inbox_pr_review`) parses the URL, resolves a repo config, fetches the PR, checks only `state == "open"` (1166) and non-empty head sha (1170), then writes `output={"inbox_review": ...}` (1231).
